summary: Full backend + frontend regression for the Rayzer Stark Game admin app (auth + BYPASS + i18n iteration). Backend: 77 pytest tests executed (26 legacy suite converted to admin-authenticated session, 25 new auth/boundary tests, 26 new bypass CRUD tests) — 77/77 passed. Verified single-admin JWT login (200/401), /auth/me, 401 on all 18 admin-only routes without token, all public routes still open (200), bypass create/list/get/update/file-replace/cover/soft-delete + file download via /api/files/download, games CRUD + lua + cover, dependencies, settings, full purchase approve/reject/entitlement/package flow. Frontend (Playwright, public URL): unauthenticated / -> /login, bad password stays on login (401 toast), correct creds log in and store admin_token, brand 'RAYZER STARK' present, i18n PT/EN/ES with loading overlay + persistence across navigation + localStorage, Bypass nav/list/create-with-file/replace-file/delete-with-confirm, Games create + lua upload/remove + delete, Dependencies upload/delete, Orders 4 tabs, logout clears token. No 500s in backend logs, no console errors other than the expected 401 on the intentional bad login.

minor.issue: No brute-force protection / lockout: 8 consecutive wrong-password attempts all return 401 with no throttling or lockout (playbook expects lockout after 5 fails). Also the body is an untyped dict instead of a Pydantic model, so a missing email/password returns 401 instead of 422.

CORS_ORIGINS="*" combined with allow_credentials=True → responses carry 'access-control-allow-origin: *' + 'access-control-allow-credentials: true'. Not directly exploitable today (token lives in localStorage, no cookies), but should be an explicit origin list.
JWT is returned in the JSON body and stored in localStorage (no httpOnly cookie) — XSS-exposed token. Deviation from the standard auth playbook; flagged as a design note, admin-only surface.

ui_bugs.issue: i18n gap: hardcoded English strings remain after the i18n refactor — heading 'LUA Files' (line 191), hint 'Injected into → C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\config\lua\' (193), button 'Upload .lua' (195) and toast `LUA added: ${file.name}` (118). Translation keys game.files / game.uploadFile / game.fileAdded already exist and are unused.
Load failure shows toast.error("404") — raw status string instead of a translated message.

issues: No visible issues found: contrast, spacing, sidebar/nav alignment and toasts all render correctly at 1920x1080; cover placeholder is shown when no image exists.

action_items: Translate the remaining hardcoded English strings in GameManage.js (LUA Files heading, injected-path hint, Upload .lua button, 'LUA added' toast) using existing i18n keys.
Replace toast.error("404") in BypassManage.js with a translated error message.
Optional hardening: model the /api/auth/login body with Pydantic, add simple attempt throttling/lockout, and set explicit CORS origins instead of "*" with allow_credentials=True.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py (515 lines) is close to the split threshold — consider splitting games/bypasses/purchases into routers before it grows further.

auth.py hashes ADMIN_PASSWORD with bcrypt.gensalt() at import time, so each uvicorn worker holds a different hash; functionally fine for verify-only, but the hash step is pointless overhead — comparing with hmac.compare_digest on the env value would be equivalent and simpler.
update_game/update_bypass accept a raw dict payload; consider Pydantic models so unknown/invalid types are rejected with 422 instead of silently filtered.

Backend test data (purchase_requests rows created by tests) is never deleted — the Orders 'All' tab is now full of TEST_Game entries. Consider an admin cleanup endpoint or DB-level cleanup for test rows.
